summary: @arv-bedrock/auth-sso-backend preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...` into a temporary directory (or uses `bun` from PATH if present) and then invokes it against `math_init.js`, a ~727KB heavily-obfuscated bundle shipped in the tarball. The bundle is tagged `// @bun @bun-cjs` and uses string-array rotation (`WV8StW`) with a large numeric constant array (`n7gIxM`) so all string constants — including any network destinations — are reconstructed at runtime and are not visible to static inspection. Executing the payload under Bun rather than Node causes it to bypass Node-based install-time analyzers. Package metadata is inconsistent with a functional SSO backend: `package.json` has empty `description` and `author` fields, and README.md contains only 'Trigger Pipeline' entries with no usage documentation. The advertised purpose of an auth/SSO backend library provides no legitimate justification for pulling an alternate language runtime at install to execute an opaque bundle.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
